question: What timeline did Juniper Cloud Tools agree for their evaluation?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract any timeline, deadline, or schedule agreed for the evaluation, including start and end dates, decision dates, trial or pilot durations, and next-step milestones, along with who agreed to them.
assumptions: Question refers to the single call with Juniper Cloud Tools (CALL-010), a Prospect technical evaluation.

findings.speaker: Marcus Chen
findings.quote: We want a four-week evaluation starting immediately, with a go/no-go decision in September.
findings.context: Juniper wants a four-week evaluation starting immediately, with a go/no-go decision in September. — Marcus states the timeline; Ava confirms start is Monday. Stated by customer.

findings.speaker: Ava Sinclair
findings.context: 'Starting immediately' means the evaluation starts Monday, with Ava having blocked time. — Clarification of the start date by the customer engineer; Leo then agrees not to spend two weeks arranging it.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: The evaluation runs four weeks from Monday against four criteria
findings.context: Leo Grant summarises the evaluation as running four weeks from Monday. — Vendor restatement of the agreed timeline.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: You'll have all four by Friday.
findings.context: OrbitFlow commits to delivering the requested items by Friday, with the three exported definitions sent earlier that afternoon. — Vendor deliverable deadlines agreed for start of evaluation; Nina accelerates the definitions.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: You'll have it in week two.
findings.context: Pricing model to be in writing in week two, before the evaluation ends. — Leo commits to a pricing timeline after Marcus requests it before the evaluation ends.

findings.speaker: Marcus Chen
findings.quote: Friday for your four things, Monday we start.
findings.context: Juniper's own deliverables (Linear backlog analysis, Salesforce API allocation, EU contract check) were assigned, with Friday as the implied deadline for the four vendor items. — Customer-side actions agreed; the Friday deadline explicitly refers to the vendor's four items.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Built by business operations, not engineering. Engineering time logged and extrapolated.
findings.context: Success criteria evaluated at the end of the four weeks, including comprehensibility test and logged engineering hours. — End-of-evaluation milestone; the criteria are agreed in the call.

draft.answer: Juniper Cloud Tools agreed a four-week evaluation starting Monday, with a go/no-go decision in September [C1][C2]. OrbitFlow's four deliverables are due by Friday, before the Monday start [C3]. Pricing is promised in writing in week two [C4]. Success criteria are assessed at the end of the four weeks [C5].

claims.text: Marcus Chen (VP Business Operations) said Juniper wants a four-week evaluation starting immediately, with a go/no-go decision in September. Ava Sinclair clarified 'immediately' means Monday, and Leo Grant restated it as four weeks from Monday.
Start date is Monday; Ava Sinclair has blocked time for it.

OrbitFlow (Nina Patel) committed to deliver all four requested items by Friday; Marcus summarised it as 'Friday for your four things, Monday we start.' The three exported definitions were to be sent earlier that afternoon.
Leo Grant committed to provide the pricing model in writing in week two, before the evaluation ends.
Success criteria, including a comprehensibility test (built by business operations, not engineering) and logged engineering hours, are evaluated at the end of the four weeks.

not_covered: The exact September date for the go/no-go decision is not given.
